title: COP31 collapses without a deal after EU and Panama reject text that omits fossil fuels
dek: The Antalya summit, the longest in UN climate history, ended on Sunday with its main decision not adopted. Existing commitments under the Paris Agreement stand.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Sunday without adopting its main decision, after the European Union and Panama formally objected to a final text that did not mention fossil fuels. It is the first time since the Copenhagen summit of 2009 that a COP has broken up without its central agreement, according to reports.

"It is clear that there are parties in this hall who oppose this text," Murat Kurum, the COP31 president and Türkiye's environment minister, told the closing plenary on Sunday afternoon, Antalya time. "We recognize that there is no consensus on this document. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted." UN climate decisions are taken by consensus, so a formal objection from any party is enough to block them.

## What happened

The two-week meeting, scheduled for 9 to 20 November, ran two days into overtime, making it the longest UN climate summit on record, beyond the overrun at COP25 in Madrid in 2019, according to reports. The hosts had circulated three drafts of a cover decision, called the Antalya Pact, in an effort to bridge the gap between countries that wanted a clear commitment to move away from coal, oil and gas and major oil producers that opposed any such language.

A call to "phase out" fossil fuels was dropped from the second draft and did not return in the third, which was published in the early hours of Sunday. The ten-page final text did not use the words "fossil", "oil", "coal" or "phase-out", according to reports. Instead it reaffirmed "in its entirety" the UAE Consensus agreed at COP28 in Dubai in 2023, the only UN climate decision that calls on countries to transition away from fossil fuels.

Ireland's climate minister, Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU, which Ireland currently chairs, said the bloc and its member states objected because the text "does not meet the moment". The EU "will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels", he said, according to reports. Panama also formally objected, and other delegations spoke against the text.

## What the rejected text said

According to reports on the final draft, the Antalya Pact would have:

- acknowledged for the first time in a COP decision that global warming is on course to exceed the 1.5°C limit set in Paris in 2015, with a long-term aim of bringing temperatures back below it
- kept a Turkish proposal to raise electricity's share of the world's final energy use to 35 per cent by 2035, and to cut methane and other non-carbon dioxide gases
- kept a goal of 1 billion tonnes a year of carbon capture, utilisation and storage by 2035, with the verb changed from "accelerate" to "scale up" in Sunday's revision
- called for faster development of technologies that remove carbon dioxide from the air
- reaffirmed a pledge to at least triple adaptation finance for developing countries by 2035, without setting a baseline or a path to get there

Campaigners had attacked the draft before the vote. Sara Shaw of the campaign group 350.org called it "a licence to keep polluting", and Berk Butan of Greenpeace Türkiye said campaigners could not accept "a tepid compromise that dodges a phaseout of fossil fuels", according to reports.

## Where India stood

India did not make a public statement at the closing plenary that could be found by the time of writing. In its national statement on 18 November, delivered by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav as head of the delegation, India asked the presidency to keep the talks grounded in equity, climate justice and the principle of "common but differentiated responsibilities", under which richer countries that have emitted most in the past are expected to do more.

"Equitable access to the remaining, depleted, carbon budget is non-negotiable," Mr Yadav said, according to reports of the statement. He said the Global Stocktake, the Paris Agreement's five-yearly review, should inform countries rather than impose obligations on them, objected to unilateral trade measures that penalise developing countries, a reference to the EU's carbon border tax, and said "the developed world must honestly and expeditiously discharge their climate-finance obligations". An Indian negotiator said India has about 17 per cent of the world's population but has produced only 4 to 5 per cent of cumulative global emissions, according to reports.

Reports during the final days named Saudi Arabia, Russia and India among the countries understood to oppose any decisive reference to phasing out fossil fuels, and said attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya to delay the next major reports of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change had become another source of friction. India has not publicly set out its position on the phase-out paragraph, and these accounts could not be confirmed from Indian government statements.

## Background

COP31 was shaped by an unusual deal between Türkiye and Australia, which had both bid to host it. Under a compromise reached at COP30 in Belém last year, Türkiye hosted the summit and Mr Kurum served as COP president, while Australia's climate minister, Chris Bowen, presided over the formal negotiations.

The fossil-fuel question has divided every summit since Dubai. At COP30 in Belém, countries agreed to work on a plan for the transition away from fossil fuels and set an aim of at least $120 billion a year in adaptation finance by 2035. In Antalya, the hosts tried to keep both camps on board by referring back to the Dubai text without repeating its wording, and the attempt failed.

## What it means

The collapse does not cancel any existing commitment. The 2015 Paris Agreement, the decisions of earlier summits, including the UAE Consensus, and the technical and legal rules that govern UN climate action all remain in force, according to reports. What is lost is the new political package the hosts had hoped would push countries to act faster before their next round of national climate plans.

For India, the outcome leaves open two issues it pressed in Antalya: the size and source of adaptation finance for developing countries, and how far the Global Stocktake can be used to set expectations for individual countries. Adaptation money matters most to countries with low-lying, cyclone-exposed coasts, among them India and Bangladesh, which share the Sundarbans delta at the mouth of the Ganga.

## What happens next

The presidency did not immediately say whether it would try to reconvene the parties or carry the unfinished items forward. Under UN rules, items that are not agreed are normally taken up again at the next session. Negotiators meet next at the UN's mid-year technical talks in Bonn in June, and the next summit, COP32, is due to be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 2027.

## Key numbers

- 2 days: overtime before the closing plenary, the longest COP on record
- 3: drafts of the Antalya Pact circulated by the presidency
- 0: mentions of "fossil", "oil" or "coal" in the final draft
- 35%: proposed share of electricity in world final energy use by 2035
- 1 billion tonnes: proposed annual carbon capture goal for 2035
